summary: Immune TTP from the ICU perspective: suspect it from thrombocytopenia, microangiopathic haemolysis and a normal coagulation screen, send ADAMTS13 activity and antibody before plasma (PLASMIC score as a bridge only), and start plasma exchange and steroids within hours with rituximab and caplacizumab once TTP is confirmed or strongly likely. HERCULES (modest primary outcome, large secondary composite benefit, more mucocutaneous bleeding) is supported by retrospective cohorts with historical controls; ISTH 2025 made no change to its conditional caplacizumab recommendation. Check troponin and ECG in everyone, avoid platelet transfusion unless life-threatening bleeding (observational evidence), and follow ADAMTS13 after discharge. Recombinant ADAMTS13 is preferred for congenital TTP; MAYARI exchange-free treatment (registry results only) does not apply to critically ill patients.
takeaways: Suspect TTP with thrombocytopenia, haemolysis and a normal coagulation screen; send ADAMTS13 activity and antibody before plasma but do not wait for the result.
Phone the TTP centre and start plasma exchange and steroids within hours, adding rituximab and caplacizumab once TTP is confirmed.
Check troponin and ECG in everyone, and avoid platelet transfusion unless there is life-threatening bleeding.
Monitor ADAMTS13 after discharge, because relapse can be silent.
